curriculum.lesson_evidence: Looking after teeth, hands and skin keeps us healthy. Teeth: brush for two minutes twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, spit out the toothpaste without rinsing, limit sugary food and drinks and visit the dentist. Hands: wash, dry and keep nails short and clean. Skin: protect it from the sun, keep it clean, cover cuts with a clean plaster and tell an adult if a cut or rash looks sore or red.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a two-minute tooth-brushing plan that covers all the teeth, with the parts of the mouth in order.

FEEDBACK
Sample: 30 seconds for each of four areas (top outside, top inside, bottom outside, bottom inside), including the chewing surfaces, then a gentle brush of the tongue. Spit but do not rinse so the fluoride stays on the teeth.

WATCH FOR
Thinking you only need to brush when your teeth feel dirty. Brushing twice a day removes the sticky plaque that causes holes in teeth.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Make a one-week care chart for teeth, hands and skin with morning, afternoon and night tasks. Tick it each day, time two tooth-brushing sessions and write what you would do if you had a small cut and who you would tell.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example daily care routine. Morning: brush teeth for 2 minutes (a timer helps) and put sunscreen on uncovered skin. Afternoon: wash hands before snacks. Night: brush teeth, spit and do not rinse, then look at hands and nails. When Ben gets a scrape he rinses it, tells an adult and covers it with a clean plaster.

TRY FIRST
Write a two-minute tooth-brushing plan that covers all the teeth, with the parts of the mouth in order.

FEEDBACK
Sample: 30 seconds for each of four areas (top outside, top inside, bottom outside, bottom inside), including the chewing surfaces, then a gentle brush of the tongue. Spit but do not rinse so the fluoride stays on the teeth.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.

teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
